items.title: 67256_Paul L. Howard oral history interview
items.q: The transcript mentions Mrs. Mabel Gray as president of Five and Over Charity Club in a news report context, but the interviewee (Paul L. Howard) does not mention her or interact with her.

ctx.x: Mr. Johnson, head of the local musicians union informed a news reporter yesterday, Friday, that he had filed with the public defender in the interest of Elmer Fain and his Musical Bees a claim for salaries owed to them for playing for the dance.

The musicians contend they were not paid. The names of Chauncy Hylen and George Henderson appeared on the citation slips, a defendant. According to Mrs. Mabel Gray, president of Five and Over Charity Club, the organization advertised as a charity beneficiary that at press time had not received one penny from the promoters.
No officials of the Businessmen's Social Club, advertised promoter of the dance, could be located for a statement.
